prompt: Make FrozenHolder effectively immutable: its constructor stores a defensive copy of the given list and getItems() returns an unmodifiable view that rejects changes.
explanation: Storing the caller's list reference would leave a back door: the caller could keep mutating it after construction. A defensive copy (new ArrayList<>(items)) snapshots the contents, and Collections.unmodifiableList wraps the copy in a read-only view whose mutator methods all throw UnsupportedOperationException. Together they make the holder effectively immutable without copying on every getItems() call.
hints: In the constructor, copy with new java.util.ArrayList<>(items) into a private final field.
Storing the parameter reference directly fails the test where the caller mutates the original afterwards.
getItems() should wrap the field with java.util.Collections.unmodifiableList(...) -- the view reads through but rejects add/remove.
